culture.localTip: Carry cash — many small shops are cash-only. Bow slightly when greeting.
culture.funFact: Tokyo has more Michelin-starred restaurants than any other city on Earth.

culture.localTip: Bargaining is expected in the Grand Bazaar. Always accept the tea offered by shopkeepers.
culture.funFact: Istanbul is the only city in the world that straddles two continents — Europe and Asia.

culture.localTip: Tip 18–20% at restaurants. Walk fast on sidewalks — stay right, pass left.
culture.funFact: New York City has 468 subway stations — more than any other city in the world.
culturalDos: Hail cabs by raising your arm
Hold doors for people behind you
culturalDonts: Stand still in the middle of the sidewalk
Take photos of strangers without asking

culture.localTip: Always greet shopkeepers with 'Bonjour' when entering. The French value politeness above all.
culture.funFact: The Eiffel Tower grows about 15cm taller in summer due to thermal expansion of the iron.

culture.localTip: Bargain at markets. The local train is the city's lifeblood — rush hour is not for the faint-hearted.
culture.funFact: Mumbai's Dharavi is one of the most productive slums in the world, generating over $1 billion annually.
culturalDos: Use your right hand for giving/receiving

culture.bestSeason: May–September (dry season) or Feb for Carnival
culture.localTip: Cariocas (Rio residents) are warm and physical — hugs and cheek-kisses are normal greetings.
culture.funFact: Rio's Christ the Redeemer statue is struck by lightning an average of 6 times per year.
culturalDos: Learn a few words of Portuguese

culture.localTip: Bargaining in the souks is mandatory — start at 30% of asking price.
culture.funFact: The University of Al-Qarawiyyin in nearby Fez, founded 859 AD, is the world's oldest continuously operating university.

culture.localTip: Australians value informality — don't be too formal. Outdoor culture is huge; beaches are free and public.
culture.funFact: Sydney Opera House has over 1 million roof tiles and took 14 years to build, finishing in 1973.
culturalDonts: Call it a 'shrimp on the barbie' (it's prawn)

culture.bestSeason: Spring (April–May) for tulips and mild weather
culture.localTip: Cycling is the dominant mode of transport — stay out of bike lanes. Almost everyone speaks English.
culture.funFact: Amsterdam has more bicycles than residents and over 1,500 bridges crossing its famous canals.
culturalDos: Rent a bike to explore like a local
culturalDonts: Photograph sex workers in the Red Light District

culture.localTip: Locals dine late — restaurants fill up after 9pm. Pickpockets are common on Las Ramblas.
culture.funFact: Gaudí's Sagrada Família has been under construction since 1882 and is still not finished.
culturalDos: Learn a few words of Catalan
culturalDonts: Be loud after midnight in residential areas

culture.bestSeason: Spring (April–May) for cherry blossoms or Fall (October) for foliage
culture.localTip: T-money cards work on all transit. Elders are given seats on public transport — always.
culture.funFact: Seoul has the world's fastest average internet speed and more Michelin-starred restaurants per capita than Paris.
culturalDos: Use two hands when giving/receiving items
culturalDonts: Write names in red ink (associated with death)

culture.localTip: Fines are strictly enforced — no chewing gum, no eating on the MRT, no littering. Singlish is an art form.
culture.funFact: Singapore is the world's only island city-state and one of only three remaining city-states globally.
culturalDos: Use hawker centres for cheap amazing food

culture.localTip: Dress modestly in public areas and malls. Public displays of affection can result in fines.
culture.funFact: The Burj Khalifa is so tall that you can watch the sunset from the base and then take the elevator to see it set again.
culturalDonts: Eat or drink in public during Ramadan

culture.bestSeason: Summer (June–August) for warmth and long days
culture.localTip: Stand on the right of escalators. Queuing is a national religion — never skip it.
culture.funFact: London's underground (the Tube) is the world's oldest metro system, opening in 1863.
culturalDonts: Make eye contact with strangers on public transit

culture.bestSeason: Spring (late March–April) for sakura or Autumn (November) for maple foliage
culture.localTip: Geishas (Geiko) in Gion are working — not tourist photo ops. Respect their space.
culture.funFact: Kyoto has over 1,600 Buddhist temples and 400 Shinto shrines — more per square kilometer than any city on Earth.
culturalDonts: Talk on the phone at temples

culture.localTip: Table Mountain is best visited early morning to avoid cloud cover. Always lock car doors.
culture.funFact: Cape Town is home to two oceans — the Atlantic and the Indian — meeting at Cape Point.
culturalDos: Take the cable car up Table Mountain

culture.localTip: Never touch someone's head or point feet at people or sacred objects. The monarchy is deeply revered.
culture.funFact: Bangkok's full ceremonial name is 168 characters long — the world's longest city name.
culturalDos: Wai (bow with hands pressed together) as a greeting
culturalDonts: Touch a monk as a woman

culture.bestSeason: March–May (dry season, warm before the rains)
culture.localTip: Mexico City is at 2,240m altitude — give yourself a day to adjust. Uber is safer than street taxis.
culture.funFact: Mexico City is sinking at about 50cm per year because it was built on a former lake bed.
culturalDos: Greet everyone individually in a group
Try street food from busy stalls (safer than quiet ones)

culture.bestSeason: Spring (March–May) — Mardi Gras season is February/March
culture.localTip: Tip your street musicians — they are the heartbeat of the city. Second lines happen spontaneously.
culture.funFact: New Orleans is below sea level — the city is protected by an 800-km network of levees and floodwalls.
culturalDos: Let the jazz wash over you
Walk the French Quarter at night safely on main streets

culture.localTip: Book the Colosseum online — queues can be 3 hours. Afternoon light is magical for photos.
culture.funFact: Rome has more obelisks than Egypt — 13 vs Egypt's 9 remaining ones.
culturalDonts: Sit on the Spanish Steps with food

culture.localTip: Vienna's Kaffeehäuser (coffee houses) are UNESCO-listed culture. Sit for hours — no one will rush you.
culture.funFact: Vienna was once the center of the Habsburg Empire — the city influenced all of European classical music.
culturalDos: Attend a concert at the Musikverein
culturalDonts: Eat at tourist traps near the Opera

culture.localTip: Czech Republic has some of the best beer in the world and it's cheaper than water in most pubs.
culture.funFact: Prague's Old Town was never bombed in WWII — it survived virtually intact, making it a living medieval museum.
culturalDos: Pay in Czech Koruna not Euros
Walk across Charles Bridge at dawn
culturalDonts: Take taxis from the street (use apps)
Miss the astronomical clock at noon

culture.localTip: Soak in a thermal bath — Budapest has 118 natural hot springs under the city. Széchenyi is the most famous.
culture.funFact: Budapest was two separate cities — Buda and Pest — until 1873 when they merged with Óbuda.
culturalDos: Try a ruin bar in the Jewish quarter
Take the funicular up to Buda Castle
culturalDonts: Ignore the Hungarian toasting ritual (eyes contact when clinking)
Skip the Parliament building at night

culture.localTip: Take Tram 28 through Alfama for the most scenic route in Lisbon — go early to avoid crowds.
culture.funFact: Lisbon is built on seven hills and is the westernmost capital city in continental Europe.
culturalDonts: Miss the sunset at Miradouro da Graça

culture.localTip: Berlin's club scene runs Thursday to Monday. Berghain has a notoriously selective door — dress down, not up.
culture.funFact: Berlin has more museums than rainy days per year — over 170 in total.
culturalDos: Respect bike lanes (never walk in them)
culturalDonts: Assume Berlin is like the rest of Germany

culture.greeting: Γεια σου (Ya sou) / Γεια σας (Ya sas — formal)
culture.localTip: The Acropolis is best visited at opening (8am) or 2 hours before closing. Evening light is spectacular from Filopappou Hill.
culture.funFact: Athens has been continuously inhabited for over 3,400 years — making it one of the world's oldest cities.
culturalDos: Greet with a cheek kiss between friends
Explore Monastiraki flea market on Sundays
culturalDonts: Visit the Parthenon at midday in summer
Assume all ancient sites are free

culture.localTip: Use an Octopus card for all transit. The Star Ferry across Victoria Harbour is one of the world's great commutes for HK$3.
culture.funFact: Hong Kong has one of the world's highest concentrations of skyscrapers — over 550 buildings taller than 150m.
culturalDos: Learn 'M̀h gōi' (excuse me / thank you) in Cantonese
Try dai pai dong street stalls
culturalDonts: Call it part of mainland China casually

culture.localTip: The Shilin Night Market is touristy — try Raohe Night Market for a more local experience.
culture.funFact: Taipei 101 was the world's tallest building from 2004 to 2010. Its tuned mass damper is visible to tourists.
culturalDos: Give up your seat on the MRT (it's strictly observed)
Accept business cards with two hands

culture.greeting: 毎度 (Maido) — the Osaka merchant greeting
culture.localTip: Dotonbori at night is iconic. Osaka is significantly cheaper than Tokyo for food — eat everything.
culture.funFact: Osaka is known as Japan's kitchen (天下の台所) — the city's motto is literally 'eat till you drop' (kuidaore).
culturalDos: Stand on the left on Osaka escalators (opposite to Tokyo)
Be loud and funny — Osakans love it
culturalDonts: Be too formal (Osakans are very casual)

videos.label: 4K Ho Chi Minh City Night Walk

culture.localTip: To cross the street, walk slowly and steadily — the motorbikes will flow around you. Never stop suddenly.
culture.funFact: Ho Chi Minh City has over 8 million registered motorbikes — roughly one per person.
culturalDonts: Refer to it as Saigon to locals who prefer the official name

culture.localTip: Porteños (locals) eat dinner at 10pm and socialise until 3am. Don't be surprised if restaurants are empty at 8pm.
culture.funFact: Buenos Aires has more psychiatrists per capita than any other city on Earth — more than New York or Vienna.
culturalDos: Greet with a single kiss on the cheek
Learn a few tango moves in San Telmo
culturalDonts: Skip the bookshop El Ateneo Grand Splendid

culture.localTip: Toronto is one of the world's most multicultural cities — every neighbourhood has a distinct flavour. Spend time in Kensington, Chinatown, Little Italy and Greektown.
culture.funFact: Toronto's PATH underground walkway is the world's largest underground shopping complex — 30km of tunnels.
culturalDos: Say sorry (it's genuine, not a cliché)
culturalDonts: Visit the CN Tower without booking ahead in summer

culture.bestSeason: Summer (June–August) — spring and fall are beautiful too
culture.localTip: Chicago's 'L' train (the elevated rail) is the best way to see the city skyline for the price of a transit ticket.
culture.funFact: Chicago was rebuilt almost entirely after the Great Fire of 1871 — the result is one of the world's greatest collections of modern architecture.
culturalDos: Walk the Riverwalk along the Chicago River
Try Giordano's deep dish — call it a casserole if you want
culturalDonts: Call it 'The Chi' unless you're a local
Diss the Cubs OR the White Sox around fans

culture.localTip: Miami is actually two cities — Miami Beach (the island) and Miami proper (the mainland). Most visitors want Miami Beach.
culture.funFact: Over 70% of Miami residents speak Spanish as their primary language — it's the only major US city where English is not the dominant language.
culturalDos: Visit Wynwood Walls for street art
Eat Cuban food in Little Havana
culturalDonts: Skip the Art Deco Historic District

culture.bestSeason: Year-round — spring and fall are ideal (72°F / 22°C)
culture.localTip: LA runs on cars. Use Waze not Google Maps. Traffic is a genuine lifestyle — podcast your commutes.
culture.funFact: LA is the entertainment capital of the world — it produces more content than any other city, with over 90,000 production sets per year.
culturalDos: Hike Runyon Canyon for city views
Explore beyond Hollywood (Silver Lake, Venice, Koreatown)
culturalDonts: Ask someone if they're an actor (everyone is)
Walk in places designed for cars
Expect things to be close — LA is enormous

culture.localTip: Bargaining is essential in Khan el-Khalili bazaar. Start at 30% of the asking price. Drink the offered tea — it's hospitality.
culture.funFact: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the only ancient Wonder of the World still standing — and it was the world's tallest structure for 3,800 years.

culture.localTip: Nairobi has the world's only national park within a city — you can see lions with the skyline behind them.
culture.funFact: Nairobi is Africa's Silicon Savannah — it's the tech startup capital of the continent, home to M-Pesa (mobile money used by 96% of Kenyans).
culturalDos: Try a matatu (minibus) ride for the full experience
culturalDonts: Walk alone at night in unfamiliar areas
Assume African cities are all the same

culture.bestSeason: August (Fringe Festival) or winter (atmospheric and uncrowded)
culture.localTip: The Edinburgh Festival Fringe in August is the world's largest arts festival — the city transforms completely. Book accommodation a year ahead.
culture.funFact: Edinburgh Castle sits on an extinct volcano called Castle Rock that erupted 350 million years ago.
culturalDos: Climb Arthur's Seat for panoramic views
Do the Royal Mile on foot
Try a whisky tasting in the Old Town
culturalDonts: Assume all Scots eat haggis daily

culture.currency: Cuban Peso (CUP) — tourists often use USD/EUR informally
culture.localTip: Cuba has two types of restaurants — state-run (mediocre) and paladares (private, family-run, excellent). Always find a paladar.
culture.funFact: Havana has the world's largest collection of classic American cars — 1940s and 50s Chevrolets and Buicks still used as taxis.
culturalDos: Respect the extraordinary resilience of the people

culture.localTip: Copenhagen is the cycling capital of the world — 62% of residents cycle to work daily. Rent a bike on day one.
culture.funFact: Copenhagen's Noma restaurant has been rated the world's best restaurant four times — the city pioneered New Nordic cuisine.
culturalDos: Cycle on the correct side of bike lanes
Visit Tivoli Gardens in the evening
